title: 5.8.13 Lab: Reap the dead with filter
description: Dead enemies stay in the array, so the list never shortens and the next hit lands on a corpse. Build a new list of the living with `filter` and store it back in `enemies`.

steps.title: Keep only the living
steps.instructions:
`filter` builds a new array from the ones that pass a test; it does not change the old array. Use it to keep the enemies where `isAlive()` is true, and store the result back in `enemies`. Put it after the hit check and before the loop.

Press Space six times. Every enemy starts with 4 hp and each hit takes 2, so it takes two presses to finish one: the counter at the bottom should go 3 → 2 → 1 → 0, dropping on every second press, and each press should hit a living enemy.
hints: The shape is in 3.7.20 (Worked Example: Chaining `.map()` off a `.push()`-Built Array): `curved.filter((score) => score >= 80)` keeps the scores that pass the test. Here that is `enemies = enemies.filter((e) => e.isAlive());`.
`filter` hands back a new array, so writing `enemies.filter(...)` without `enemies =` throws the result away.

requirements.title: A filtered list is stored back in enemies
requirements.description: `filter` is used and its result is assigned back to `enemies`, so the array itself gets shorter. Help: 3.7.20 (Worked Example: Chaining `.map()` off a `.push()`-Built Array)

requirements.title: The test keeps the enemies that are still alive
requirements.description: The filter keeps the living — it asks each enemy `isAlive()`, or compares its health. Help: 3.7.20 (Worked Example: Chaining `.map()` off a `.push()`-Built Array)
